items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: Let's see, the bass player was Nick Finton, and the saxophone player's name was Scotty.

ctx.x: And I just always heard like this, you know. So as I say, it was just a gift, I guess, you know. But coming back to Charlie Christian, I heard Dizzy say -- Dizzy's the only one who really tells the truth about -- I don't say tell the truth. Who really is aware what happened. I never tried

to play like Charlie Christian. I've been given credit for playing like Charlie or being influenced by Charlie, but I never -- I always admired his playing, he was a tremendous guitarist. But we thought differently, and I would go to hear Charlie every night in Minton's. That's when Dizzy was there, and Joe Guy and Monk. Let's see, the bass player was Nick Finton, and the saxophone player's name was Scotty.

And every night I would go there because Charlie would come by and play, and I admired his play. But I never wanted to play like him, because I heard different things, you know. His was a very exciting style and everybody just loved him, including me. And all the guitarists just jumped on his style. But I had to be me, and I guess I'm stubborn, you know.
